questionText:
Solve for x (correct to TWO decimal places):
2x² + 1 = 4x
modelAnswer: Standard form: 2x² − 4x + 1 = 0. Quadratic formula: x = [−(−4) ± √((−4)² − 4(2)(1))] / (2×2) = [4 ± √8]/4 → x = 1,71 or x = 0,29 (correct to two decimal places).
hint: Rearrange to standard form, then the quadratic formula.

questionText: Solve for x (correct to TWO decimal places): 3x² + 1 = 6x
explanation: Standard form: 3x² − 6x + 1 = 0. Quadratic formula: x = [6 ± √(36 − 12)]/6 = 1 ± √6/3 ≈ 1 ± 0.8165 → x ≈ 1.82 or 0.18. Re-seeded numbers of the official NSC structure — machine-verified.
hint: Standard form, then the quadratic formula.
